title: I tested 4 strategy families out-of-sample, found no edge, and built guardrails for AI trading agents instead (free, open)
author: GabrielGauss

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: in-sample Sharpe of 1-2 dropping to between -1.5 and 0.4 is the result almost nobody posts. one pushback on the survivor: daily BTC from 2022 is maybe two regimes, so I'd trust the drawdown gap from vol targeting and hold the Sharpe gap loosely.

replies.author: GabrielGauss
replies.body:
Yeah its fair, and I agree. You pushed me to actually check. Correction first: the timing strategies ran 2022–2026, but the vol-target test used daily data from 2018, out of sample from 2020-01 (13 walk-forward folds, \~2,370 days). Still only a few regimes.

I ran a paired block bootstrap on the stitched OOS returns (10k resamples, 5/21/63-day blocks, all similar). The Sharpe gap (1.03 vs 0.85) has a 95% interval of roughly −0.4 to +0.7, and \~28% of resamples show no improvement. So it isn't distinguishable from zero, as you suspected.

The drawdown reduction holds up better: 41.6% vs 76.0%, with the ratio's interval at about 0.4–1.0, so it's rarely worse than holding. But it misses my pre-set "under 75% of buy and hold's drawdown" bar in about a quarter to a third of resamples. And that's before accounting for parameter re-selection between folds. In the last fold it picked no trend filter and fell 28.1% alongside BTC's 28.6%.

The same procedure also failed on ETH (Sharpe 0.81 vs 0.89). I've added the bootstrap to the write-up in the repo. Honest summary: a somewhat smoother way to hold BTC, with weaker evidence than my post implied. thank you

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: 2018 to 2026 with 2020 and 2022 inside it is a better spread than I gave you credit for, a crash and a slow grind down test vol targeting in very different ways. a block bootstrap on the stitched OOS is about as honest as one sample gets. I'd still read the drawdown gap as the result and the Sharpe gap as a maybe.
